inputMonitoring.title: Input Monitoring
inputMonitoring.description: Required so Vox Jot can better tell the difference between sending a message and manually clearing text.

Keep correction tracking local to this device.
inputMonitoring.privacy: Does not log what you type or store your keystrokes.

screenRecording.title: Screen Recording
screenRecording.description: Required so Vox Jot can build a rolling OCR cache from the active display and use it as local dictation context.

bullets: Read active-screen context for better dictation accuracy.

Improve phrase keys and app-aware writing.
screenRecording.privacy: Only used for local context features; you can skip this and enable it later.

permissions.privacyBadge: Vox Jot runs dictation on your device. We never upload your voice, keystrokes, or screen context.

refine.title: Want a local Refine engine?
refine.description: Refine polishes dictated text after transcription — cleanup, formatting, or rewriting. For fully local Refine, Vox Jot can install Ollama and a small model now. You can skip this and set it up later.

bullets.optional: Optional. You can skip now and configure any Refine provider later.

refine.footnote: If you skip, Refine still works once you connect a cloud provider in Settings > Models & AI.
refine.cardDescription: Refine runs after transcription to clean up filler words, fix punctuation, or rewrite in a tone.

welcome.title: Set up private voice dictation that actually fits your workflow
welcome.description: Vox Jot lets you speak into any app, keeps transcription local on your device, and can optionally polish the final text before it is pasted.
welcome.cardDescription: Get the core flow working first, then tailor the output once you know how you want Vox Jot to behave.
features: Download a local speech model that matches your speed and accuracy needs.
Grant the permissions Vox Jot needs to listen and type into other apps.
Learn the regular dictation shortcut now and configure polished dictation later if you want it.

Adjust output, paste behavior, or polished dictation later from Settings.

dataPrivacy.introTitle: How Vox Jot handles your data
dataPrivacy.introBody: Speech is transcribed on your device using the models you install. Optional AI post-processing may run on-device (for example Apple Intelligence) or through a provider you configure. Transcript history and retention limits apply only to data stored locally on this computer—nothing is sent to Vox Jot’s servers because there is no cloud account.

screenContext.intro: When you dictate, Vox Jot can glance at what's on screen and run on-device OCR so the refine pass understands names, tabs, and field labels you were looking at. Captures stay on your Mac.

screenContext.exclusionsDescription: Vox Jot will never capture the screen while one of these apps is frontmost. Great for password managers, banking, or any app you want kept private.
screenContext.addCurrentAppFailed: Couldn't detect a frontmost app to exclude.
screenContext.ocrEngineDescription: Pick which engine reads text from screen captures. The default uses your operating system's built-in OCR and falls back to the cross-platform engine if it fails.
screenContext.ocrEngineHelpLinux: Linux always uses the cross-platform engine — install `tesseract` and `grim` (Wayland) or `import`/`gnome-screenshot` (X11).
screenContext.ocrEngineHelpWindows: Windows uses Windows.Media.Ocr by default and falls back to Tesseract when the system OCR fails or returns empty results.
screenContext.ocrEngineHelpMacos: Apple silicon Macs always use Apple Vision; the cross-platform engine is reserved for QA and Intel-Mac experiments.
